topics.description: Brazilian politician who served as president of Brazil from 2019 to 2022.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country filed charges against an expatriate American journalist who reported on leaked  documents from this country's Operation Car Wash investigation. During COVID, this country's  president promoted chloroquine treatments and personally contracted the disease at least three  times. That president accused environmental organizations of starting 2019 (*) fires that plagued  this country's rainforests. For 10 points, name this South American country where a 2022 election pitted  former president Lula da Silva against incumbent Jair Bolsonaro (jai-IR bowl-so-NAR-oh).
parts.answer: ANSWER: Brazil [Federative Republic of Brazil; or República Federativa do Brasil]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Voters in this country overwhelmingly rejected a radical constitution which included 388 new articles. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this South American country, led by President Gabriel Boric.
parts.answer: Chile [or Republic of Chile; or Republica de Chile]

parts.label: B
parts.question: Every single Chilean province rejected the proposed new constitution, including this strongest base of support for Boric, the capital city of Chile.

parts.label: C
parts.question: This President was lambasted by Chile for accusing Boric of committing “acts of arson.” This former President of Brazil controversially called COVID-19 “a little flu.”

topics.description: A Comorian politician who served as president of Comoros from 2006 to 2011 and was nicknamed “Ayatollah.”

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about the Moissy, or the time Comoros had a secret police made up of teenagers. For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: The Moissy were trained in this country south of Kenya, which is near Mount Kilimanjaro.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Since they were teenagers and ran by a 15-year-old, the Moissy were annihilated when this country invaded  Comoros. This country was once led by Charles de Gaulle.
parts.answer: France [or the French Republic; or République française]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Comoros’ first peaceful transfer of power occurred in 2006 when a man with this nickname was elected. An  unrelated man with this title issued a fatwa against Salman Rushdie in 1989.

topics.description: The socialist Yugoslav federation led by Josip Broz Tito from 1945 until its dissolution during the Yugoslav Wars in the early 1990s.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This country distanced itself from the Soviet Union during the Informbiro Period. For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this country that broke up in 1992. It was led from 1953 to 1980 by Josip Tito, who led its resistance to fascism during the Second World War.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] After a 1941 coup d’etat (koo dey-TAH), Yugoslavia was invaded by this military alliance. This group of countries, which included Germany, Japan, and Italy, fought against the Allies in World War II.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] During World War II, Yugoslav resistance forces consisted of the Yugoslav Partisans and the Chetniks, nationalists from this country. Slobodan Milosevic led this country during the Kosovo War.

topics.description: The former Balkan country and broader Yugoslav state that existed in several political forms, including the kingdom, communist federation, and later successor state formations.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This country was organized into communes called opštine under a system called “workers’ self￾management.” This country’s Informbiro period followed World War II, during which the royalist Chetnik movement and the fascist Ustaše [oo-stah-sha] operated. A leader of this country who threatened “If you don’t stop sending killers, I’ll send one to Moscow” was the only European signee at the Bandung Conference for the (*) Non-Aligned Movement. This country fell apart when Slobodan Milošević [mil-OH-suh-VICH] rejected self-determination for Slovenes and Croats in the 1990s. Josip Broz Tito was the Cold War leader of, for 10 points, what former Balkan country?
parts.answer: Yugoslavia [accept Kingdom of Yugoslavia; or Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia; or Federal People’s Republic of Yugoslavia; accept Yugoslav Wars]

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Political prisoners in this country were held in a labor camp located on the island of Goli Otok. A leader of this country promoted the slogan “Brotherhood and unity” among this country’s various ethnic groups. This country became a republic after its last king, Peter II, was deposed following World War II. A leader of this country initiated its (*) Informbiro period following a split with the Soviet Union. That leader of this country served as the first chairman of the Non-Aligned Movement, of which this country was the only European founding member. This country was led by Slobodan Milosevic during its violent breakup in the 1990s. For 10 points, Josip Broz Tito led what former country located in the Balkans?
parts.answer: Yugoslavia [or Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia or Kingdom of Yugoslavia]

topics.description: Martin Luther's 1517 propositions criticizing the sale and theological basis of indulgences and helping initiate the Protestant Reformation.
aliases: Disputation on the Power and Efficacy of Indulgences

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This man wrote the hymn "A Mighty Fortress is Our God." This man debated Huldrych Zwingli (HULL-drick TSVING-lee) at the Marburg Colloquy and was excommunicated by Leo X at the Diet of Worms (vorms). This man's anger at Johann Tetzel's sale of indulgences prompted him to (*) nail his most famous work into the door of a church in Wittenberg. For 10 points, name this author of the 95 Theses who started the Protestant Reformation.

topics.description: Structures or sites used for burial, including graves, burial monuments, mausoleums, tumuli, and royal or monumental burial complexes.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A painted silk banner depicting Lady Dai and her attendants was discovered in one of these structures called Mawangdui. A keyhole-shaped type of these structures lends its name to the Kofun period of ancient Japan. Central Asia is home to many of these structures called kurgans, which are a type of tumulus. The high levels of (*) mercury detected around one of these structures give credence to Sima Qian’s (“shee-ma chi-AN”) claim that it once contained rivers of mercury. One of these structures in Xi’an (“shi-AN”) dedicated to Qin Shihuang (“chin shee-HWANG”) contains an army of terracotta warriors. For 10 points, name these structures in which people are buried.
parts.answer: tombs [or mausoleums or graves or burial mounds or líng; accept tumulus or tumuli before “tumulus” is read; accept kurgan before “kurgan” is read; accept necropolis]

topics.description: A German Catholic military order active in the Crusades and Northern Europe, including the Baltic region, and associated with the 1242 Battle on the Ice.
aliases: Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem
Order of the Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem

parts.label: L
parts.question: Valdemar Atterdag plundered the city of Visby during his war with this organization. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this trade confederation that operated trading posts called kontors in cities like Lübeck. This trade confederation was active in Northern Europe, especially the Baltic.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] Valdemar Atterdag was the king of this country that was eventually forced to sign the Treaty of Stralsund with the Hanseatic League. Valdemar was the first king of this country to rule from its current capital of Copenhagen.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] Valdemar earlier sold the province of Danish Estonia to this other organization. This organization had previously lost the 1242 Battle of the Ice to the forces of Novgorod under Alexander Nevsky.
parts.answer: Teutonic Knights [or the Teutonic Order or Order of Brothers of the German House of Saint Mary in Jerusalem; prompt on the Livonian Order with “what larger organization was it part of?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: The classroom doodlings of the boy Onfim (OHN-feem) were excavated in this city, which was the  site of a 1570 massacre ordered by Ivan (ee-VAHN) the Terrible. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this former Hanseatic (HAN-zee-AH-tik) city whose namesake northern republic, controlled  by the elected veche (vee-ETCH-eh), was the last major competitor to Moscow in Russia.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Novgorod (NAHV-guh-rod) [or Veliky Novgorod; do not accept or prompt on “Nizhny  Novgorod”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Novgorod was founded by the Varangian (vaa-RAN-ghee-un) prince Rurik, whose son Oleg  founded this other Rus (ROOS) city. The original Rus state was named for this now-Ukrainian city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Alexander Nevsky, a 13th-century prince of Novgorod, defeated this crusading order of German  speakers at the Battle on the Ice in 1242.

topics.description: Warsaw is the capital and largest city of Poland, historically significant as the site of the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising and as the namesake of the Warsaw Pact.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: After the destruction of this city, so-called “Robinson Crusoes” hid in its ruins for over three  months. Groups such as the ZOB, which operated a bunker at Miła (MEE-wah) 18, fought Jürgen  (YORG-en) Stroop's forces in this city. A forest near this city was the site of a facility built under  Operation Reinhard in the village of (*) Treblinka (treb-LINK-ah). Chłodna (WOHD-noh) Street was  an enclave within this city, which in 1939 had the largest Jewish population in Europe. For 10 points,  name this Polish city where Jews launched a 1943 uprising against the Nazis from a designated ghetto.

topics.description: The ancient Roman amphitheater in Rome, commissioned under the Flavian emperors and used for gladiatorial contests, animal hunts, staged naval battles, and other public spectacles.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One commander revived the use of decimation during a rebellion of these people. Under Decimus, a group of these people hid in the Theater of Emperor Commodus. Secutors and Murmillos were two types of these people, which contrasted with the trident and net-wielding retiarii. The pollice verso was a (*) thumbs-down signal given to these people. The Third Servile War began under an escaped one of these people named Spartacus. Titus sponsored the mass killing of lions and rhinos by these people in the Flavian Amphitheater. For 10 points, name these slave warriors who fought in the Colosseum.
parts.answer: gladiators [prompt on slaves with “What specifically was their job?”]

topics.description: A country in Western Asia centered on Mesopotamia, with Baghdad as its capital and a history including the Iran-Iraq War and the First Gulf War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: Ironically, violence escalated in this country after a president gave a speech about it under a "Mission Accomplished" banner. Because of tensions over oil, this country invaded its neighbor to begin the First Gulf War. In 1980 this country invaded (*) Iran under the leadership of Saddam Hussein. The terrorist group ISIS is named for Syria and, for 10 points, what country led from Baghdad?
